## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
This maintenance visit recorded a critical deficiency in pump operation. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed equipment failure requiring immediate professional attention. All other system components measured within normal parameters.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |
| Liquid Level | At Outlet |

The effluent filter was cleaned and reseated during this visit. Filter condition was good with light soiling.

## PUMP OPERATION
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | CRITICAL - No Load |

**Finding:** The pump motor is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated full-load amperage. This indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic load. Possible causes include a dry-running condition (no fluid reaching the pump), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. Continued operation without load will cause motor overheating and damage.

**Alarm Status:** High water alarm tested functional.  
**Electrical Connections:** Sound.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
Surface condition is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE:**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. A qualified technician must examine the pump discharge line for disconnection or blockage, check the impeller for damage or absence, and verify that fluid is reaching the pump inlet. Do not continue operating the pump in its current no-load condition.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored and verified.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Operation
The effluent pump is the heart of your aerobic treatment system. It moves treated liquid from the tank to the dispersal field. When the pump runs without hydraulic load -- that is, without actually moving fluid -- the motor overheats rapidly and fails. The low amp draw recorded during this visit is a clear sign that something is blocking or preventing fluid flow. This is not a minor issue and should not be deferred. Contact a qualified technician today.

### Solids Management
This maintenance visit recorded solids at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids accumulate naturally over time as bacteria break down waste. Keeping non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, medications -- keeps that accumulation slow and predictable.
